question.text: Mr. Verma, aged 68, wants to avail a reverse mortgage. The property he intends to offer as security is a commercial shop in a market complex, of which he is the sole legal owner (he lives in a separate flat that he does not wish to mortgage). Per the workbook (pp. 118-119), can he avail a reverse mortgage on this commercial shop?

answer.text: Yes, since he is above 60 years of age and is the sole legal owner of the property
Yes, provided he obtains a no-objection certificate from the local municipal authority
No, because reverse mortgage cannot be availed against commercial property - the property must be a residential property used as the borrower's permanent primary residence
Yes, provided he converts the commercial property to residential use within 6 months of disbursal

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pp. 118-119), reverse mortgage can be availed ONLY against a residential property that is the borrower's permanent primary residence; a reverse mortgage loan cannot be availed against commercial property. Mr. Verma's shop is commercial, and he does not live in it - so it fails BOTH the "residential" and "permanent primary residence" requirements. Option C is uniquely correct. The Trap: Options A, B and D each invent a workaround (ownership alone, municipal NOC, conversion clause) that the source does not allow. Candidates who focus on the borrower's age or ownership status miss that the property type itself is the bar. Note: The original stem described a shop-cum-residence (mixed-use), but the workbook (pp. 118-119) does not directly discuss mixed-use property treatment or partial residential valuation. The stem has been narrowed to a purely commercial property held by a borrower who lives elsewhere, so the keyed answer "No - reverse mortgage cannot be availed against commercial property" is directly supported by the workbook. Source: NISM Series-X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook, pp. 118-119.
